theater: 尼羅河三角洲東岸與黎凡特濱海

battle.name: 與施爾登海盜的衝突
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲東岸與黎凡特濱海
battle.brief: 約公元前1278年，拉美西斯二世在王位第二年，率埃及軍沿尼羅河三角洲東岸與黎凡特濱海迎擊舍爾登人的船隊。來犯者反覆用夜間靠岸、破門掠奪再退回海上的手法，埃及則靠海岸堡壘、烽火接力與封死內陸路口把襲擊擋回去。戰況多靠梅內普塔碑與阿瑪爾納書簡回推。卡面月牙劍是埃及舊式彎刃，此時已讓位給直刃短劍。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場衝突的交戰方，一方是埃及新王國第十九王朝，一方是以舍爾登為首的沿海武裝集團。埃及方面由法老拉美西斯二世直接統帥，軍隊以皮拉美西斯為基地，沿尼羅河三角洲東岸與黎凡特濱海佈防：步兵以阿蒙、拉、普塔、塞特四師為骨幹，配弓箭手大隊、雙馬戰車部隊與專司海岸警戒的巡邏隊，另有各城邑的守備民兵與傳遞烽火的守望隊；河口堡壘與沿岸關隘構成第一道線。舍爾登一方並非國家，而是散居東地中海、以船隊為核心的戰鬥團體，首領各自帶隊，多數受雇為傭兵兼掠奪者，部分乾脆以劫掠為生；在阿瑪爾納書簡的年代，他們已被黎凡特城邦雇來作戰與破壞。夾在雙方之間的是迦南、基利、推羅等西奈及黎凡特沿岸諸邦：誰出錢，誰就可能換到舍爾登人的箭。埃及在北方要守住的，正是這些城邦的港口、穀倉與商路。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the nineteenth-dynasty New Kingdom of Egypt and a loose body of coastal fighters headed by the Sherden (Šerden). On the Egyptian side the command was the pharaoh's own: Ramesses II ruled the host directly, basing it at Pi-Ramesses and covering the eastern edge of the Nile Delta together with the Levantine seaboard. The backbone of the army was the four infantry divisions — Amun, Ra, Ptah and Seth — supported by a body of archers, a chariot corps, and a watch of patrols assigned to the coast; alongside them stood the garrison of each town and the beacon crews of the watchtowers, and the fortresses at the river mouths and the passes inland made the first line. The Sherden were not a state but a set of war bands scattered around the eastern Mediterranean, each led by its own chief; most hired themselves out as mercenaries while raiding on the side, others lived outright on plunder, and by the age of the Amarna letters they were already being employed by the Levantine city-states as soldiers and as spoilers. Caught between the two were the states of Canaan, Cilicia, Tyre and the rest of the Syrian coast: whoever paid would get Sherden arrows. What Egypt had to hold in the north was precisely those cities' harbours, grain stores and caravan roads.
people: 拉美西斯二世是這場衝突的中心人物。他前一二七九年即位，前一二七八年已是王位第二年，仍在鞏固三角洲與北方邊界的階段；他也正是數年後在卡迭石與赫梯對峙的同一位法老。真正把舍爾登人的名字帶進埃及檔案的是他的兒子梅內普塔：前一二〇八年，梅內普塔在東三角洲的卡爾納克立碑，記錄第五年擊敗利比亞聯軍時，敵方名單上出現「舍爾登」與「舍爾登號」戰船，這份名單可說是舍爾登人最完整的一次點名。書吏阿蒙斯在梅內普塔第八年所刻的卡爾納克守軍銘文裡，記錄了被俘後分派到埃及軍隊與要塞服役的舍爾登人。再往前，阿瑪爾納書簡中，耶路撒冷統治者阿布迪-希巴與阿穆魯的沙爾瑪尼先後寫信給埃及，抱怨舍爾登人出現在那一帶；這些書信是舍爾登人最早的文字足跡。
peopleEn: Ramesses II is the central figure of this conflict. He had taken the throne in 1279 BC, so 1278 was his second regnal year, and he was still consolidating the Delta and the northern frontier; he was the same king who would face the Hittites at Kadesh a few years later. It was his son Merneptah who put the name of the Sherden into the Egyptian record: in 1208 BC, in the stele he set up at Karnak in the eastern Delta, Merneptah recorded the defeat of the Libyan coalition in his fifth year, and the enemy list carries both the Sherden and a Sherden ship — the fullest single naming of the group that survives. The scribe Ahmose, whose Karnak garrison inscription belongs to the eighth year of Merneptah, recorded Sherden captives being posted to the Egyptian army and to the fortresses. Further back, the Amarna correspondence shows Abdi-Heba of Jerusalem and Šalmani of Amurru complaining in turn to Egypt about Sherden men appearing in their country; those letters are the earliest written trace of the name.
kits: 卡面這把埃及月牙劍是最典型的埃及式彎刃單手劍，刃背向外凸、刀口內彎，砍進去不必拔出來。它自早王朝起就是埃及步兵的制式短刃，到中王朝仍是軍中最常見的兵器。但到了拉美西斯二世這個年代，實際裝備已經換成直刃短劍：梅迪奈特哈布與卡爾納克的浮雕以及出土兵器都顯示，埃及步兵多持直刃的塞赫姆式短劍，月牙劍的形制在軍中退居次要，只在部分守備隊與鄉間部隊手上還留有殘餘。同期上陣的還有埃及的複合弓與箭、長矛、斧、投石索、輕型雙馬戰車，以及用來封鎖河口與護航的船隻。舍爾登那邊的裝備簡陋而耐用：短劍、長柄斧、近身用的短矛、可投擲的標槍、角弓與箭，以及最關鍵的圓盾——從梅吉多、泰勒哈達爾、泰勒沙姆霍納與泰勒法拉等遺址出土的帶雙橫把手陶片，被考古學界視為舍爾登式圓盾的實物線索。梅迪奈特哈布的浮雕裡，海上民族的戰士戴圓頂盔、頸束毛皮，這些形象通常歸給提克人與佩萊塞特人，尚無法確定哪一部分屬於舍爾登。
kitsEn: The khopesh on the card is the archetypal Egyptian curved single-edged sword, its back bowed outward and its edge curving inward, so that a blow did not have to be twisted out of the wound. It had been the standard short blade of the Egyptian infantry since the early dynastic period and was still the commonest weapon in the army of the Middle Kingdom. By the time of Ramesses II, however, the actual issue had changed to straight-edged short swords: the reliefs at Medinet Habu and Karnak and the excavated weapons show Egyptian infantry carrying straight sekhem-type blades, and the khopesh form had dropped to a secondary place in the line, surviving only in the hands of some garrison troops and country levies. Also on the Egyptian side were the composite bow and its arrows, spears, axes, slings, light two-horse chariots, and the river craft used to close the mouths of the Nile and to escort shipping. The Sherden were equipped more plainly but durably: short swords, long-handled axes, short thrusting spears, javelins, bows of horn, and above all a round shield — the sherds with two horizontal lug handles found at Megiddo, Tel Hadar, Tel Shiqmona and Tell el-Far'ah are treated by archaeologists as the physical trace of the Sherden round shield. In the reliefs of Medinet Habu the seaborne warriors wear domed helmets with a ruff of fur round the neck; those figures are usually assigned to the Tjekker and the Peleset, and it cannot be said with certainty which of them were Sherden.
tactics: 舍爾登人的戰法有一套反覆出現的樣板：多半趁順風夜間或清晨駛近岸邊，挑城邑最薄弱的牆段靠岸登陸，先破城門、放火掠奪，再在埃及援軍趕到之前退回海上，必要時以船上的弓手與投石手壓制城頭。埃及一方的應對，是把防線攤在整條海岸上：河口堡壘與燈信首先發現來敵，沿途烽火台接力把警報送到三角洲的皮拉美西斯；戰車部隊在後方道路集結待命，步兵封死通往內陸的路口；弓箭手依托城牆與土壘覆蓋灘頭，務求不讓對方帶著戰利品退回水裡。追擊同時走陸路與海路兩條線：駐軍沿沙丘與鹽鹼地追蹤，船隊則在外海攔截企圖重新集結的敵船。這類衝突的勝負，往往不取決於一次野戰，而取決於警報傳得多快、封路的兵力夠不夠。
tacticsEn: The Sherden followed a repeated pattern: they would use a following wind to run in by night or in the early morning, choose the weakest stretch of a town's wall, put their boats ashore, break the gate, set fire and plunder, and then withdraw to the water before Egyptian reinforcements could arrive, using the archers and slingers in their boats to cover the wall while they did it. Egypt's answer was to spread the defence along the whole coast. Fortresses and signal fires at the river mouths picked the movement up first and passed the alarm along the line of watchtowers to Pi-Ramesses in the Delta; the chariot corps was assembled in the rear on the roads; the infantry sealed the tracks that led inland; and the archers, posted behind the walls and earthen banks, covered the beachhead, so that the raiders could not carry their plunder back to the water. The pursuit ran on two lines at once: detachments tracked the raiders over the dunes and salt flats, while the ships themselves intercepted hostile craft trying to re-form beyond the shoals. The outcome of such a clash rarely turned on a single field battle; it turned on how fast the alarm travelled and on whether enough men could be put in the way.
data: 關於這場衝突，可靠的數字非常有限，可查證的只有以下幾組。其一，阿瑪爾納書簡的年代約在前一三五〇年前後，自地中海東岸諸城邦寄往埃及埃及其他宮廷的信件，路上要走約一至三個月；這說明海盜式的襲擊傳到法老耳中時，往往已是事件發生數月之後。其二，與舍爾登相關的戰役規模，可由梅內普塔第五年碑的量級衡量：同年埃及人自述擊敗利比亞人與其盟友，敵方除利比亞步兵外，還有數千名海民步兵，並有一艘「舍爾登號」大船在海戰中撞毀一艘埃及船；同一塊碑上記載的埃及軍力在萬人上下，戰車以千計。其三，考古層面上帶雙橫把手陶片的數量在數百件之譜，集中於梅吉多、泰勒哈達爾、泰勒沙姆霍納等沿海地點，說明這些戰士的數目並非可以忽略的小股。至於前一二七八年那一天究竟出動多少人、交戰多久、以何種方式收場，沒有任何一份當時的戰報留下數字；本文所記月份與部署，都是依古埃及的遠征季節與海戰條件所作的重建。
dataEn: Reliable figures for this clash are few, and only a handful of groups of them can be established. First, the Amarna letters date from around 1350 BC, and a letter travelling from the city-states of the eastern Mediterranean to the Egyptian court took roughly one to three months on the road; a piratical raid would therefore reach the pharaoh's ears months after the event. Second, the scale of Sherden fighting can be read off the fifth-year stele of Merneptah: in that year the Egyptians claimed to have beaten the Libu and their allies, with several thousand seaborne infantry in the enemy host and a Sherden ship that rammed and destroyed an Egyptian vessel in the fighting; the Egyptian force described on the same monument is of the order of ten thousand men and a thousand or more chariots. Third, the number of lug-handled sherds runs to several hundred, clustered at coastal sites such as Megiddo, Tel Hadar and Tel Shiqmona, which shows that these fighters were not a handful of men. As for how many troops were committed on the day in 1278 BC, how long the fighting lasted, and in what way it ended, no contemporary report gives a single number; the month and the deployments given here are a reconstruction from the Egyptian campaigning season and the conditions of a fight at sea.
cause: 把這場衝突推到前一二七八年的，是幾條同時收緊的線索。東地中海的青銅資源在十三世紀前後急遽吃緊，黎凡特與塞浦路斯的礦區日漸枯竭，銅與錫的交換比例惡化，長途海上貿易的利潤被壓薄；一批失去生路的船主與失了土地的戰士轉而以武力掠奪為生，這正是所謂「海上民族」的經濟底色。與此同時，埃及自阿瑪爾納書簡年代起便把迦南與西奈視為屏障，拉美西斯二世即位之初要做的，正是把北方的海岸線與港口控制在自己手裡，擋住這類船隊。而年代更早的敍利亞城邦已經學會購買這類戰士：阿布迪-希巴與沙爾瑪尼的信件裡，舍爾登人既是受雇的打手，也是不聽招呼的破壞者。於是衝突的性質很清楚：一方是試圖維持既有秩序的王朝，一方是靠邊際收益過活的武裝集團；傳統編年把前一二七八年記為拉美西斯二世「擊敗施爾登人」的一年，正是把這場長期的邊境摩擦，壓縮成一個可以記錄的年份。
causeEn: Several threads tightening at once pushed this conflict back to 1278 BC. Bronze resources in the eastern Mediterranean ran short sharply around the thirteenth century: the mines of the Levant and of Cyprus were worked out, the exchange ratio between copper and tin worsened, and the margin on long-distance sea trade was thinned; boatowners who had lost their living and landless warriors turned to force as a means of living — that is the economic base of what are called the Sea Peoples. At the same time Egypt, from the age of the Amarna letters onward, had treated Canaan and the Sinai as a shield, and what Ramesses II needed to do at the opening of his reign was to hold the northern coastline and its harbours in his own hand and bar the way to such fleets. And the Syrian city-states had already learned to buy this kind of fighter: in the letters of Abdi-Heba and Šalmani the Sherden appear both as hired swords and as spoilers who would not take orders. The nature of the clash is therefore plain — a dynasty trying to hold an existing order against an armed group living on marginal returns — and the traditional chronology compressed this long friction on the frontier into a single datable year, 1278 BC, remembered as the year in which Ramesses II defeated the Sherden.
impact: 若把視線放長，這場衝突的真正重量並不在前一二七八年的那一役，而在其後兩百年間地中海東岸秩序的崩解。舍爾登人沒有被消滅，只是從掠奪者變成了傭兵：梅內普塔的碑文裡出現被俘後編入埃及軍隊的舍爾登人，拉美西斯二世本人也曾以舍爾登人作近侍。同一批人於是既能替埃及守城，也能替別的城邦攻城，幾乎任何一方的軍陣裡都可能出現他們的身影。到了塞納克特與拉美西斯三世時期，海上民族大舉登陸，一度席捲自迦薩至尼羅河三角洲的海岸，最後被壓回海上；但黎凡特的城市、港口與存貨已經耗盡，晚期青銅時代的舊秩序隨之崩潰，舊約的記載與「出埃及」的敘事正是在這個背景下成形。另一方面，這場缺乏戰報的衝突在後世被不斷放大：十九世紀以來，學者把「海上民族」這個統稱與各個名字綁在一起，寫出了一整部歐亞大陸邊界崩潰的通史；而本卡所承載的傳統編年，只是這部大敘事裡一個最簡潔的節點。
impactEn: Put into a longer frame, the real weight of this clash does not rest on the engagement of 1278 BC itself but on the collapse of order along the eastern Mediterranean in the two centuries that followed. The Sherden were not destroyed; they turned from raiders into mercenaries. Merneptah's stele records Sherden captives posted into the Egyptian army, and Ramesses II himself used Sherden men as personal attendants. The same men could therefore guard an Egyptian city or lay siege to another, and they might turn up in almost any line of battle in the region. In the reigns of Setnakhte and Ramesses III the seaborne peoples landed in force, swept the coast from Gaza to the Nile Delta, and were finally driven back into the water; but the cities, harbours and stores of the Levant had already been spent, the old order of the Late Bronze Age collapsed with them, and the narratives of the Old Testament and of the Exodus took shape against that background. The clash, which left no report of its own, has meanwhile been magnified by later writers: since the nineteenth century scholars have welded the general term Sea Peoples to these separate names and written a general history of the collapse of Eurasia, and the traditional date carried by this card is only the tidiest node in that larger story.
result: 以傳統編年的說法，這一場以埃及取勝收場：拉美西斯二世在王位第二年驅散了在黎凡特與三角洲東岸活動的舍爾登船隊，把海岸線與港口的防衛重新握回法老手中。但就史料而言，結果其實沒有這樣整齊：前一二七八年沒有留下任何一份當時的戰報、損失表或俘獲名單，雙方的部署、交戰過程與數字都只能由後來的文件回推。更可確定的是，衝突並未因此終止——阿瑪爾納書簡裡舍爾登人已出現在敍利亞城邦的軍隊中，梅內普塔第五年他們又作為利比亞聯軍的一員被擊敗並列入戰俘名冊，其後在拉美西斯三世的戰役中仍有殘敵被清剿。換言之，埃及贏得的是一場沒有條約收尾的邊界戰鬥：海民沒有被趕出地中海，而是從敵人變成可用可棄的武力；這條海上通道，要到青銅時代崩潰之後才真正失去威脅。
resultEn: On the traditional chronology the affair ended in an Egyptian victory: in his second regnal year Ramesses II broke up the Sherden fleets working along the Levant and the eastern Delta and took the defence of the coast and its harbours back into the pharaoh's hands. On the evidence, however, the result was not so tidy. No report, casualty list or roster of prisoners from 1278 BC survives, so the deployments, the course of the fighting and the numbers on both sides can only be reconstructed from later documents. What can be asserted is that the conflict did not end there. In the Amarna letters the Sherden were already serving in the armies of the Syrian city-states; in Merneptah's fifth year they were beaten again as part of the Libyan coalition and written into the roster of captives; and in the campaigns of Ramesses III there were still remnants to be hunted down. Egypt had won, in other words, a border fight closed by no treaty. The sea peoples were not driven out of the Mediterranean: they turned from an enemy into a force that could be used or discarded, and that sea lane only truly ceased to be a threat after the collapse of the Bronze Age.
